scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported Anguilla polygon spans 1715 to 2020. The narrative includes earlier archaeology and later heritage documentation as explicitly dated context. It does not treat the polygon as proof of Indigenous territory or the 2020 endpoint as extinction.

The AAHS cave account was read. Deity identifications are interpretations, and bowl form and find context support rather than prove ritual use. No blanket Indigenous disappearance claim or claim of current UNESCO World Heritage inscription is adopted.

Petras’s October 2021 report was read in its introductory, Locus SH and Locus C sections. Architectural functions and identities of occupants remain tentative. Page 14 describes Wilson’s measurement, while the report distinguishes ship-carving interpretation from specific historical events.

The 1834 boundary follows the cultural-policy appendix and the report’s emancipation compensation discussion. It is not a claim that every form of labor coercion or inequality ended at once. The 1700 plantation boundary is approximate.

The cultural-policy historical appendix, pages 17 to 19, was consulted on gov.ai after the stats.gov.ai mirror had a certificate problem. Its idealized community narrative is not used as a universal demographic survey, and its claims of complete Indigenous absence and cultural stripping are not repeated.

Salt and boat gallery captions were read. No unobserved visual detail, wage, individual worker identity or ship cargo is inferred. The 1902 date belongs specifically to Warspite, not every boat displayed.

The British Library series catalog was consulted. Individual lighthouse journal and provision-ledger pages were not transcribed; the card does not invent their contents. AAHS and National Trust activity is distinguished from guaranteed preservation outcomes.

The 1967 revolution and 1980 separate territory status are distinguished from sovereign independence. The current UN profile identifies the administering power. No current officeholder or invented successor polity is supplied.

The government history compresses association chronology; the card separately dates federation membership and collapse and avoids assigning associated statehood to 1962. Its uncertain Columbus and naming claims are omitted.
Independent historical review, border assessment and depth certification remain pending.
